name: fig_final_clean_test_success_and_seed_outcomes.jpg
caption: Simulated closed-loop drone racing results on two clean test sets the method was never tuned on (seeds 141-156 and 161-176, 16 random tracks each, 4 drones per track, 64 flights per arm per test). A flight succeeds if the drone passes all 22 gates without crashing. Only the gate detector differs between the arms: GateNet (baseline) or ours (frozen core plus CornerRefiner, CornerPeakHead, NearGateHead, global duplicate suppression and a 14 px minimum box size filter). (a) Success rates with 95% Wilson intervals and success counts. Ours reaches 87.5% in both tests, against 81.2% and 82.8% for GateNet, and 87.5% against 82.0% over all 128 flights (+5.5 points). The intervals overlap, and the y-axis starts at 60%. (b) Per-seed outcomes: a seed counts as a win if ours completes more of its 4 flights than GateNet, a loss if it completes fewer, and a tie if both complete the same number. Ours wins more seeds than it loses in both tests (6/2/8 and 6/3/7 wins/losses/ties; 12/5/15 combined). A sign test on the combined result, excluding ties, gives p ~ 0.14. The improvement points the same way in both tests but is not significant at p < 0.05. Hatched bars show the combined results.

name: fig_incloop_corner_error_vs_gate_size.jpg
caption: Median in-loop corner error in pixels for detected frames only, comparing the simulation-trained GateNet baseline (solid blue) with our frozen core at step B (hatched orange). Step B is the frozen core plus synthesized single-corner peaks. Results come from closed-loop Isaac Lab simulation, and the y-axis uses a log scale. For small gates (0–60 px), GateNet has 0.79 px error and ours 2.65 px (×3.4). For large gates (>250 px), the errors are 9.4 px and 26 px (×2.8), so the error grows with apparent gate size. The inset gives the overall values across all gate sizes: median 0.97 vs. 3.5 px (×3.6) and p90 3.3 vs. 16.5 px (×5.0). The green band marks the roughly 1–2 px corner precision the EKF state estimator needs. Both detectors find the gate in these frames, so the closed-loop gap comes from corner pixel precision rather than recall.

name: fig_development_path_success_rate_progression.jpg
caption: Closed-loop success rate (%) of the frozen-core gate detector at each development step (A–F), in Isaac Lab simulation only. Each track is a random 22-gate course flown by 4 drones per seed, and a flight succeeds only if all gates are passed without a crash. Blue circles are measurements on clean, never-used seeds. Filled orange diamonds are measurements on validation seeds 41–56, which were used only to choose settings. Hollow diamonds show the val_H result on the same validation seeds and the min-size sweep (min8, min20) on seeds 41–48. Dashed grey segments show GateNet, a detector trained only in simulation, wherever it was evaluated on the same seeds. Grey bands show the estimated loop noise of ±10 and ±15 points for 32 flights. Starting from 37.5% against GateNet's 78.1% (A), synthesised corner peaks (B), the CornerRefiner (C, no measurable loop gain) and the CornerPeakHead and NearGateHead (D) narrow the gap to about 10 points. Adding small near-gate detections without deduplication collapses success to 15.6%, because duplicate detections of one gate break the EKF. Global duplicate suppression (E) adds 14.0 points on validation and reaches 82.8% against GateNet's 87.5% on clean seeds 121–136. The 14 px minimum-size filter (F) reaches 90.6% on validation. In the final clean tests (128 flights), success is 87.5% for our detector and 82.0% for GateNet (sign test p ≈ 0.14).

name: fig_estimator_error_by_distance.jpg
caption: EKF next-gate position error by true distance to the gate, comparing GateNet (grey) with our frozen core plus modules (blue) in closed-loop simulation. Results come from two clean tests on never-used seeds: Test 1 (seeds 141–156, circles) and Test 2 (seeds 161–176, squares), with 64 flights per method per test. Each marker is the median error and each whisker extends to the 90th percentile (p90). Up to 8 m, the medians of both detectors are nearly the same (0.08–0.13 m), but our p90 errors are smaller. At 2–4 m our p90 is 0.27/0.26 m against 0.35/0.41 m for GateNet, a reduction of about 23–37%. At 4–8 m it is 0.30/0.28 m against 0.37/0.34 m. For far gates (8+ m), GateNet is better, with lower medians (0.21/0.20 m vs. 0.24/0.24 m) and shorter tails (p90 0.50/0.46 m vs. 0.61/0.57 m).

name: fig_edge_latency_energy_jetson_orin.jpg
caption: Median GPU latency versus total energy per frame for three backbones on a Jetson Orin NX 8 GB (TensorRT fp16, 384×384 input, batch 1, GPU compute only). Hollow markers show the 15 W power mode and filled markers show MAXN. Arrows link each model's two operating points, and labels give throughput in FPS. The dash-dot line marks the 30 Hz camera rate (33.3 ms per frame), and the shaded region is slower than the camera. The reparameterized FastViT-SA24 hybrid is the fastest and most energy-efficient model in both modes: 26.4 ms and 0.286 J at 15 W, and 14.6 ms and 0.230 J at MAXN. It is the only model that keeps up with the camera rate at 15 W. ViT-B (39.5 ms) and the plain hybrid (44.2 ms) are slower than the camera at 15 W, and all three models are faster than the camera at MAXN. The timings cover the frozen core only. The latency of the added modules (CornerRefiner, CornerPeakHead, NearGateHead and duplicate suppression) on the Orin has not yet been measured.

name: fig_ablation_duplicates_and_min_size_filter.jpg
caption: Post-processing ablation in closed-loop simulation. (a) Offline duplicate detections per frame. Adding small near-gate detections without deduplication raised duplicates to 0.317 per frame, about 17.6× GateNet's 0.018 (val_H: 0.054), and closed-loop success collapsed to 15.6 % because duplicate detections of one gate crash the EKF. Offline crop metrics such as found rate and corner order did not show this failure. (b) Validation success versus the minimum box-side filter. The selected 14 px threshold (star) reached 90.6 % on seeds 41–56 (64 flights). The 8 px and 20 px thresholds reached 81.2 % and 78.1 % on the smaller subset 41–48 (32 flights), so the comparison is not strictly matched. The dotted line marks val_DS without a size filter (82.8 %, seeds 41–56). Shaded bands show ±12 points, which reflects loop noise of about ±10–15 points at 32 flights.

name: fig_closed_loop_evaluation_pipeline.jpg
caption: Closed-loop evaluation protocol in Isaac Lab simulation (no real-flight results). Top: rendered frames pass through a fixed camera line (820×616 sensor, 128° HFOV, 30 Hz, 50 ms delay, rolling shutter with tilt error, sensor corruptions, and an adaptive 384×384 crop with derotation). A swappable gate detector then outputs 2D gate-corner observations. The detector is either the simulator-trained GateNet baseline or our frozen FastViT-SA24 core with CornerRefiner, CornerPeakHead, NearGateHead, duplicate suppression (IoU 0.2) and a 14 px minimum-size filter. An EKF fuses these observations with a map prior of the gate layout, and a learned racing policy sends control commands back to the quadrotor. Only the detector changes between arms. Bottom left: each seed generates a new random track with its own gate poses and sizes, decoys, obstacles, hall, quadrotor parameters and start pose. Four drones fly each seed for 3000 steps, and a flight succeeds only if all 22 gates are passed without a crash. Bottom right: because loop noise is about ±10–15 points for 32 flights, settings are chosen on validation seeds (31–38, 41–56) only. Results are reported on separate, never-used clean test seeds, and the final tests (141–156, 161–176) use 64 flights per arm each.

name: fig_frozen_core_plugin_module_framework.jpg
caption: Overview of the frozen general model and its plug-in modules. Left: the frozen multi-task student (FastViT-SA24 hybrid, ~8M parameters, 448 px input) runs four general heads: semantic segmentation, inverse depth, lane, and a dense gate-corner head (stride 4, size level 56, top-K 8). Its weights are never modified. Center: three small trainable modules have read-only access to the frozen stride-8 fused features. CornerRefiner refines each detected corner to sub-pixel accuracy in a second pass. CornerPeakHead (cpk3) confirms weak detections with a corner-peak heatmap. NearGateHead (ng2, threshold 0.6) detects near gates that fill the frame. Their outputs are merged with the core's initial detections (detection threshold 0.05), then passed through two steps with no learned parameters: global duplicate suppression (NMS, IoU 0.2) and a filter that drops boxes with a side under 14 px. Right: the filtered gate corners feed an unchanged third-party drone racing stack in Isaac Lab simulation, made up of an EKF state estimator and a learned racing policy. Only the detector is swapped; the baseline is GateNet. Removing the modules restores the core bit-for-bit, so general metrics cannot get worse by construction (e.g., TuSimple lane IoU 0.803, SUN RGB-D mIoU 0.749, BDD100K mIoU 0.734 are identical with and without the modules). Hatching marks frozen parts, dashed orange borders mark trainable modules, and dotted borders mark the steps with no learned parameters.
